project.objective: Did Mary E. McAndrew (G13G-P68) and her husband John Mogan of Detroit have any children besides the five already in the tree?

questions.question: Who were all the children born to Mary E. McAndrew and John Mogan of Detroit?
questions.rationale: The objective asks whether the couple had children beyond the five in the tree, which is the complete set of their children; no question covers it yet. The tree's five children were born 1876-1888, and no marriage date is recorded for the couple, so the search window is open at both ends. The tree holds no sourced evidence for any of the five yet.

items.rationale: Tree records Mary (b. 12 Jul 1848 New Brunswick) in Detroit in 1870 and her parents Bernard and Abby in Detroit in 1870 and 1880; no census is attached for the Mogan household in 1880. The 1880 schedule gives relationship to head, so it shows every child living with John and Mary then (tree children Thomas b. 1876 and John Vincent b. 1879) and any unrecorded child born 1876-1880 or dead before 1880. The 1870 schedule predates the known births and serves to locate Mary and the marriage window (no marriage date is in the tree). Check surname variants Mogan, Moogan, Mohan, Morgan, Magan and McAndrew/McAndrews. loc_001 says most Detroit census volumes are browse-only, so check each volume's searchability.

items.jurisdiction: Detroit Ward 8, Wayne, Michigan, United States
items.rationale: Tree places John, Mary, Edward, Anna Irene and Mary L. in Detroit Ward 8 in 1900. The 1900 schedule records the number of children born to the mother and the number still living, so a count above five, or a gap between born and living, signals unrecorded children, including ones who died young. loc_001 notes the Detroit 1900 volumes are largely name-indexed with images.

Mary (widowed, d. 1925) should appear in 1910 and 1920; the 1910 census again records children born and living for the mother, extending the 1900 count test to the end of her childbearing years. Tree residences: Thomas in Ward 4 in 1910, Anna Irene in Ward 10 in 1920. Detroit streets were renumbered 1 Jan 1921, which affects matching addresses across years.

The Michigan State Census 1894 (name-searchable, collection 1825187) falls in the gap left by the lost 1890 federal census, between the 1880 and 1900 schedules, and would show any child present in 1894 who is absent in both federal years.

Search for births to John Mogan and Mary McAndrew/McAndrews across Michigan, Births, 1867-1902 (1459684), Michigan, County Births, 1867-1917 (1923472) and Michigan, Births and Christenings, 1775-1995 (1675348), all name-searchable. Tree births: Thomas 1876, John Vincent 1879, Anna Irene 18 Nov 1884, Edward 31 Dec 1885, Mary L. Aug 1888. Gaps 1880-1884 and 1886-1887, and any birth after 1888, are where an unrecorded child would sit. loc_001 warns the unindexed Wayne County microfilm excludes City of Detroit and pre-1900 registration was incomplete, so a miss is weak evidence; search by parents' names with no child name.

Irish Catholic family; baptisms stand in for missing civil births. Michigan, Church Records, 1819-1991 (2787825) is name-searchable; search parents' names. Tree holds Anna Irene christened 27 May 1885 (Wayne, Michigan). loc_001 says the family's parish is not established and Archdiocese of Detroit registers (1704-1930) are on microfilm at the Burton Historical Collection; the parish named in Anna Irene's christening, once read, should be the first register browsed there. Registers are often in Latin.

Marriage of John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew: the tree has no marriage date. Search Wayne County marriage returns (indexed marriage collections) and Catholic marriage entries to fix the earliest possible birth date; if the marriage was after 1876 only, no earlier child; a marriage before 1876 opens a window for children born 1870-1876. Check surname variants. The record may also name witnesses, relatives to follow.

Death records for children who may have died young and left no census trace: Michigan, Deaths, 1867-1897 (1452402), Michigan, Deaths and Burials, 1800-1995 (1675357), Michigan Mortality Schedules 1850-1880 (2632078, for deaths in the year before the 1880 census) and Michigan, Death Certificates, 1921-1952 (1968532). Adult children's certificates (tree: Thomas d. 2 May 1924, Edward d. 16 Nov 1934, John Vincent d. 22 Sep 1950) and Mary's own (d. 31 Mar 1925) name parents and sometimes list siblings. Search parents' names as father/mother with surname Mogan. Detroit deaths before 1897 are not separately described in loc_001; Detroit deaths since 1897 sit with the Detroit Health Department.

Pre-provided capture ancestry-mi-deaths-mogan-wayneco.pdf (Wayne County death records from Ancestry): read it for Mogan decedents whose parents are John and Mary, especially children who died young or between censuses; compare with the FamilySearch death results in the previous item. Hand to search-external-sites to log the capture and record extractable facts.

Michigan, Obituaries, 1820-2006 (2215693, name-searchable) and Detroit newspapers: loc_001 notes obituaries list surviving children by name. Targets: John d. 3 May 1905, Mary d. 31 Mar 1925, Mary's mother Abby (obituaries 20 and 21 Aug 1894 are in the tree) and father Bernard (d. 12 Oct 1888), plus the adult children's obituaries. A child named as surviving who is not among the five answers the question directly.

Michigan, Probate Records, 1797-1973 (2013878) is browse-only (personCount 0), so this is an image browse of Wayne County dockets, not a name search. John d. 3 May 1905 and Mary d. 31 Mar 1925; petitions list heirs at law and are sized to the parents' deaths, not the children's births. Both testate and intestate files; the heirs list would name all living children and any grandchildren of deceased ones.

Pre-provided capture ancestry-mi-probate-mogan-john.pdf (John Mogan's Wayne County probate file from Ancestry): read for the petition's heirs list and any will naming children. Compare against the five known children; confirm this John Mogan is the husband of Mary E. before using it. Hand to search-external-sites.

Catholic cemetery interment records (Mt. Elliot, also Elmwood per loc_001; held at the Burton Historical Collection and the cemeteries) and Find a Grave. Infants buried in the family lot, or Mogan burials sharing a lot with John, Mary or her parents (Bernard d. 1888, Abby d. 1894), expose children who died young and never reached a census or obituary. Tree burials are only recorded as Detroit.

sources.transcription: PETITION FOR APPOINTME . ENT OF ADMINISTRATOR . James 11 . Stone & Co., Printers, 11 Rowland Street, TO THE HON . Edgar A. Durfee Judge of Probate for the County of Wayne, in the State of Michigan : The Petition of Charles E. Christian who is the age of twenty - one years and upwards, of the County of Wayne respectfully shows : That Sarah C. Christian departed this life on the Ninth day of November in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and ninety - six leaving no and Testament, as your petitioner is informed and verily believes . last Will Petroit That said deceased was, at the time of her death an inhabitant of the city of in said County of Wayne, that she was possessed of real and personal estate, situate and being in the County of Wayne, to be administered, and that the estimated value thereof is the sum of three thousand Dollars, or thereabout, of which three hundred Dollars is personal estate, as your petitioner is informed and verily believes . And your petitioner further shows that the names and residences of the heirs at law of said deceased, and other persons interested in her estate, are as follows : Charles E. Christian, husband of said deceased, your petition Mrs Mary E. Mogan, of full age, sister William McAndrews, aged fifteen years, replew all residents of the City of Detroit Michigan Your petitioner therefore prays to himself that administration of said estate may be granted or some other suitable person, and that such other and further order and proceedings may be had in the premises, as may be required by the statutes in such case made and provided . Dated November A.D. 1896 Charles Mohan

quirks: Statewide birth and death registration in Michigan began 1867, general compliance not reached until 1915 (FamilySearch Michigan Vital Records) - Mogan children born before ~1900 may lack filed birth records.

Detroit birth records since 1893 are obtained from the Wayne County Clerk; FamilySearch's unindexed Wayne County birth/death microfilm (1867-1917) explicitly excludes City of Detroit events, so Detroit births/deaths must be sought separately from county-wide ones.
Wayne County death index 1934-1953 held at Burton Historical Collection also excludes City of Detroit deaths; a separate Detroit Death Index (microfiche, 1920-current) covers Detroit proper.

A large number of Roman Catholic church records from the Archdiocese of Detroit (1704-1930, baptisms, marriages, deaths, first communions, confirmations) are on microfilm at the Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library - the specific parish Mary McAndrew and John Mogan attended is not established by any tool result in this survey; search broadly across Detroit's Catholic parish registers.
Detroit streets were renumbered 1 January 1921 (same house, different numbers) - affects matching addresses across census years.

volume_search found 644 digitized volumes for Detroit 1870-1930; most Vital/Death group volumes (140 of 154) are browse-only images with no name index, and most Census volumes (55 of 69) are likewise browse-only despite being ~97-100% recordSearchablePercent on some specific rolls - check each volume's own searchability rather than assuming.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan (1870-1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- Wayne County organized November 21, 1815; county seat Detroit, the oldest county in Michigan.
- Population (Wayne County): 1870: 119,068; 1880: 168,444; 1890: 257,114; 1900: 348,793; 1910: 531,591; 1920: 1,177,645; 1930: 1,888,946 (FamilySearch Wayne County Genealogy page).
- Large Irish Catholic immigrant population in Detroit in this era; parish-based Catholic recordkeeping common.
- No known courthouse record-loss disasters in Wayne County (per the wiki page).

## Boundary changes
Wayne County boundaries were established in 1815 as an original county and were stable through the 1870-1930 period; Detroit itself annexed surrounding land 1806-1926 (especially 1915-1925), which can change which jurisdiction a given Detroit address fell under historically, and streets were renumbered in 1921.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- Start date: statewide registration of births and deaths began in Michigan in 1867; general compliance by 1915 (FamilySearch Michigan Vital Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Michigan_Vital_Records). Marriage registration with the county clerk dates to 1805/county formation.
- What exists: FamilySearch "Michigan, Births, 1867-1902" and "Michigan, County Births, 1867-1917" (index & images); "Michigan, Deaths, 1867-1897" and "Michigan, Deaths and Burials, 1800-1995"; "Michigan, Death Certificates, 1921-1952."
- Where held: county level at the Wayne County Clerk for events in Wayne County generally; Detroit-specific births since 1893 come from the Wayne County Clerk, and Detroit deaths since 1897 from the Detroit Health Department. The FamilySearch Library's unindexed Wayne County birth/death microfilm (1867-1917) explicitly excludes City of Detroit events.
- Gaps: pre-1915 compliance was incomplete; Detroit deaths before 1897 are not separately described by a tool result.
- Pre-registration alternatives: church (Catholic parish) baptism/death records; obituaries; probate.

### Church records
- Denominations present: Catholic (large Irish and other immigrant population), Lutheran, LDS branches, others.
- Record types: Archdiocese of Detroit Catholic church records on microfilm at the Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library, ranging (by parish) 1704-1930 and including baptisms, marriages, deaths, first communions, confirmations.
- Where held: Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library (physical/microfilm); also FamilySearch "Michigan, Church Records, 1819-1991" (index & images, 103,627 persons) and the volume_search results show many browse-only Detroit "Church records" volumes dated 1858-1930.
- Gaps: this survey did not identify the specific parish the Mogan/McAndrew family attended; no tool result names it.
- Language: Catholic sacramental registers of this era are commonly in Latin; researcher should expect to read Latin entries.

### Census records
- Federal census: 1870, 1880, 1900, 1910, 1920, 1930 cover this period (no 1890 federal census survives generally); Ancestry links for each year were returned by external_links_search.
- State census: Michigan State Census 1894 (FamilySearch collection 1825187, 381,961 persons) and 1884 Statistical Returns (Ancestry/Findmypast).
- Access: volume_search shows several Detroit 1900 federal census enumeration volumes 97-98% name-indexed with images; overall, of 69 Census-group volumes for Detroit 1870-1930, 55 are browse-only and 2 are full-text-only, so specific rolls vary - check each volume.

### Probate and court records
- Types: wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories, petitions - held by the county probate judge.
- Testate or intestate: not established; search both wills and administration files until one is found for John Mogan (d. by 1905) and Mary E. McAndrew Mogan (d. by 1925).
- Date range: Wayne County probate records 1832-1967 (FamilySearch Catalog koha 3292257); FamilySearch "Michigan, Probate Records, 1797-1973" collection (images only).
- Where held: Wayne County Probate Court, Coleman A. Young Municipal Center, Detroit; also microfilmed estate case files 1797-1901 and probate calendar books 1797-1914 at the Archives of Michigan, Lansing.

### Land records
- Survey system: rectangular (federal) survey for Michigan generally.
- Land-distribution jurisdiction: after initial transfer from public to private ownership, subsequent transactions recorded at the Wayne County courthouse (Register of Deeds).
- Types: deeds, mortgages; FamilySearch Full-Text Search - Land Records covers variable dates/places.
- Where held: Wayne County Register of Deeds (https://www.waynecountylandrecords.com/recorder/web/).

### Military records
- Relevant conflicts: Civil War (ended 1865, veteran records continue into this period via GAR), WWI (1917-1918).
- Record types: Michigan GAR Membership Records 1876-1945; Michigan Census of WWI Veterans with Card Index, 1917-1919.
- Where held: FamilySearch collections 2351035 and 3007553; NARA for federal military/pension files.

### Cemetery records
- Major cemeteries named in the wiki page: Elmwood Cemetery (Record of Interments 1846-1992), Mt. Elliot Cemetery (1845-1997), Woodmere Cemetery (1868-1888) - held at the Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library.
- Online coverage: Find a Grave and BillionGraves both have Wayne County search pages.
- Physical records: sexton/interment records at the cemeteries themselves and the Burton Historical Collection.

### Newspaper records
- Local papers: Detroit Gazette (1817-1830) digitized at Google News; Digital Michigan Newspapers at Central Michigan University; Chronicling America has Michigan newspapers.
- Where held: digital archives as above; Ancestry's Michigan Newspapers.com Stories and Events Index, 1800s-current.
- Content value: obituaries, marriage notices.

### Obituaries
- FamilySearch "Michigan, Obituaries, 1820-2006" collection (index & images, 8,932,479 persons, id 2215693) - this is the primary named obituary index for the state and covers the full 1870-1930 window.
- Content note: obituaries in this era commonly list surviving children by name and residence, directly useful for enumerating the Mogan children.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Relevant ports: Port of Detroit (land/water border crossings from Canada).
- Record types: "Michigan, Wayne, Detroit, Manifests of Arrivals at the Port of Detroit, 1906-1956" (FamilySearch collection 1916040, 1,364,974 persons) covers only 1906 onward, so it postdates the Mogan/McAndrew Irish immigration if it occurred earlier; naturalization records (Michigan, Eastern and Western Districts, Naturalization Records, 1837-1993) may show arrival and origin information for John Mogan.
- Where held: FamilySearch/NARA RG 85 (manifests), Eastern District federal court (naturalizations).

### Tax records
- Types: county property/personal tax; no specific Wayne County tax collection was returned by these tools.
- Substitute value: can fill gaps between census years; see Michigan Taxation wiki page (not fetched in this survey).

### Other record types
- City directories: "City Directories - Detroit" 1861-1923 at Fold3; Detroit City Directory 1895 at MyHeritage - useful between censuses to track the family's address and track children aging into adulthood.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Michigan Births 1867-1902 (id 1459684); Michigan County Births 1867-1917 (id 1923472); Michigan Deaths 1867-1897 (id 1452402); Michigan Deaths and Burials 1800-1995 (id 1675357); Michigan Death Certificates 1921-1952 (id 1968532); Michigan Church Records 1819-1991 (id 2787825); Michigan Probate Records 1797-1973 (id 2013878); Michigan Obituaries 1820-2006 (id 2215693); Michigan State Census 1894 (id 1825187); Manifests of Arrivals at Port of Detroit 1906-1956 (id 1916040) | Wayne County birth/death microfilm excludes City of Detroit; Michigan Obituaries fills the gap of listing children by name | Free |
| Ancestry | Michigan Death Records 1867-1952; Michigan Wills and Probate Records 1784-1980; 1870-1930 US Federal Census years | Images where FamilySearch has index-only | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** volume_search matched 644 digitized volumes for Detroit 1870-1930 across all record types; only the first 10 were detailed above (titles), with the full by-record-type counts given in the summary (e.g., 154 Vital, 69 Census, 53 Religious, 354 Migration volumes). collections_search returned 31 Michigan-level (not Detroit-specific) collections, all listed above or omitted as out-of-scope (military, naturalization).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library | Catholic Archdiocese of Detroit church records on microfilm (1704-1930); Wayne County Marriage Returns 1803-1893; cemetery interment records (Elmwood, Mt. Elliot, Woodmere); Wayne County Death Index 1934-1953 (excludes Detroit) | In-person; some indexes online |
| Wayne County Probate Court, Coleman A. Young Municipal Center | Probate records for all of Wayne County and Detroit | In-person/mail |
| Wayne County Register of Deeds | Land records for Wayne County and Detroit | In-person/online (waynecountylandrecords.com) |
| Archives of Michigan, Lansing | Wayne County estate case files 1797-1901; probate calendar books 1797-1914 (microfilm) | In-person |

## Records NOT online
- Original Catholic parish sacramental registers (only microfilmed at the Burton Historical Collection, not digitized online per these tool results).
- Pre-1920s Wayne County tax records.
- Many probate case files/dockets - full case files largely require in-person access at the courthouse or Archives of Michigan.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey identifies any lost or destroyed Wayne County vital, probate, or court records; the FamilySearch Wayne County Genealogy page states there is no known history of courthouse disasters in this county.

## Research tips
- Search both the FamilySearch "Michigan, Obituaries, 1820-2006" collection and local Detroit newspapers for obituaries naming all surviving children of John Mogan and Mary E. McAndrew Mogan (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Michigan_Obituaries).
- Because Wayne County's unindexed birth/death microfilm (1867-1917) excludes City of Detroit events, search Detroit-specific sources (Detroit Health Department for deaths since 1897, Wayne County Clerk for Detroit births since 1893) separately from county-wide collections (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Michigan_Vital_Records).
- Search Wayne County probate records (wills if testate, administration if intestate) for both John Mogan (d. by 1905) and Mary E. McAndrew Mogan (d. by 1925); Michigan probate records in the 20th century often give an exact death date and can name heirs/children.
- Search all available federal censuses (1870, 1880, 1900, 1910, 1920, 1930) for the Mogan household; the 1880 census added relationship-to-head-of-household, useful for confirming children.
- Check the Archdiocese of Detroit Catholic parish registers (microfilmed at the Burton Historical Collection) for baptisms of children born to the couple; no tool result names the specific parish, so this will require browsing multiple Detroit Catholic parishes' baptismal registers.
- Detroit streets were renumbered 1 January 1921 - keep this in mind when tracing addresses across census years (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Wayne_County,_Michigan_Genealogy).
